claims.claim_text: The indexed Emmett F Connelly is a high-confidence match to Emmett F. Connely of Detroit, documented as an Army colonel in 1942-1943.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A July 1942 federal bulletin identifies Detroit civilian Emmett F. Connely as nominated to Army Specialist Corps field-service leadership with colonel rank; the 1943 Official Register places Col. Emmett F. Connely in the Army Officer Procurement Service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The uncommon full name and middle initial, near-exact surname, Detroit association and consistent colonel chronology across two official sources make the indexed-person match high confidence. No source directly crosswalks the printed private identifier, so the spelling difference remains visible.
claims.temporal_assessment: The official sources establish Army roles in 1942-1943 but do not establish the date or path into OSS.
claims.match_notes: The OSS index prints Connelly; the contemporary sources print Connely. The private identifier is masked and has not been used as a public crosswalk.

claims.claim_text: The last specifically documented civilian employer before Emmett F. Connely's 1942 Army appointment is First of Michigan Corporation, where a 1940 directory lists him as president.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The 1940 Investment Bankers Association directory lists Detroit president Emmett F. Connely with First of Michigan Corporation; the July 1942 federal bulletin identifies him as a Detroit civilian nominated for Army service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence indexed-person match from the uncommon full name and middle initial, near-exact surname, Detroit association and consistent transition into documented colonel service.
claims.temporal_assessment: The employer is explicit in 1940 and military entry is bounded to July 1942. Because the sources do not explicitly exclude an intervening role, the last-civilian-employer claim is medium confidence and not labeled immediate pre-OSS.
claims.match_notes: The historical Connely spelling is retained as a documented variant. A separately surfaced, undated American Securities Corporation lead is not used to displace the dated employer evidence.
